predecessors.name: Former Qin
predecessors.text: Longxi, where the Qifu were settled and where Guoren joined his uncle Butui's rebellion in 383

predecessors.name: Southern Liang
predecessors.text: the Huangshui commanderies round Ledu and Xiping, the Southern Liang's last land

successors.name: Tuyuhun
successors.text: the rest of Qin's territory: the Longxi core, Fuhan and the Huangshui land, without Nan'an

successors.name: Xia (Helian Xia)
successors.text: Nan'an, the lone city left to Mumo (the Qifu Chipan page glosses Nan'an as Dingxi, Gansu; Dingxi is not in the gazetteer, so Longxi, in that area, stands in)

ledger.x: 385: Qifu Guoren founds the Western Qin at Yongshi.
388: Qiangui, acclaimed because Guoren's son was too young, moves the capital to Jincheng (Yuzhong, near Lanzhou).
394: Qiangui takes the rest of the Former Qin's land in Longxi.

395: Qiangui takes the title King of Qin, the state becomes known as the Western Qin, and the capital moves to Xicheng; he briefly submits to Later Liang the same year (Later Liang's dossier records the submission).
400: Later Qin crushes the Western Qin.
409: Qiangui restores the Western Qin at Mount Dujian.
410: the Western Qin retakes the heartland.
412: Qiangui moves the capital to Tanjiao and is assassinated by Gongfu; Chipan defeats Gongfu, takes the throne and moves the capital to Fuhan, where it 'would remain for many years'.
426: Xia's winter attack on Fuhan forces Qifu Chipan 'to move the capital to Dinglian (also in Linxia)'.
427: 'Qifu Chipan moved his capital back to Fuhan.'
429: under pressure from the Northern Liang, Mumo moves the capital to Dinglian (modern Linxia).
430: Mumo offers to surrender to Northern Wei but Helian Ding stops him at Nan'an, which becomes the capital.
430: the Tuyuhun take the rest of the Qin.
431: Xia ends the Western Qin at Nan'an.

wars.name: Western Qin-Later Liang wars
wars.outcome: Qiangui fought the Later Liang in Hexi from 391, submitted briefly in 395 and repelled a Later Liang invasion in 397; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Later Qin conquest of Western Qin
wars.outcome: Later Qin defeats Qiangui, who flees to Southern Liang and then to Later Qin; the Western Qin is suspended until 409.

wars.name: Western Qin conquest of Southern Liang
wars.outcome: Chipan captures Ledu and the Southern Liang's last commanderies surrender; Rutan surrenders and is poisoned later in 414.

wars.name: Western Qin-Northern Liang clashes
wars.outcome: After 414 'the two sides fought with each other on multiple occasions'; Liang pressure drives Mumo to Dinglian in 429.

wars.name: Xia raid on the Western Qin
wars.outcome: Hulu Gu and Wei Fa take Nan'an and Xiping and attack Fuhan and Yuanchuan; Qifu Chipan moves the capital to Dinglian; Xia then withdraws, leaving the Western Qin 'dealt a major blow'.

wars.name: Tuyuhun and Xia conquest of Western Qin
wars.outcome: The Tuyuhun take the rest of the territory in 430; Helian Ding takes Nan'an in 431 and Xia executes Mumo; Mumo had offered to surrender to Northern Wei in 430.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier exists in the pages; every border is approximate.
